title: Lending Accrual and Fee-Allocation Consistency (Generated Value Bounds the Fee)

dasp: DASP-3 Arithmetic (accrual precision and fee rounding)

descriptions.semantic: When a lending instance accrues value over elapsed time, the post-state balances equal a declared accrual-and-allocation relation applied to the pre-state; the quantity allocated as a fee never exceeds the quantity actually generated; and the instance's notion of time, its outstanding debt, and the claims of protected creditors each move only in the directions the profile declares. The accrual relation itself is a parameter: the record requires that one be declared and obeyed, not that any particular rate model or discretization be used.
descriptions.system_theoretic: Accrual is a transition parameterized by an elapsed-time measure. The profile supplies an accrual function from pre-state and elapsed time to a generated quantity, and an allocation function distributing that quantity among claim classes. The property is the conjunction of an exactness clause (post-state equals the declared relation applied to the pre-state, with no unaccounted term), a bound clause (the fee share of the allocation is bounded above by the generated quantity), and monotonicity clauses (the time measure is non-decreasing; the debt measure is non-decreasing across a pure accrual step; protected claims do not decrease).
descriptions.security: Accrual is where a lending system creates value, and any path that creates more than the declared relation permits is an inflation bug reachable without any external actor. Four families matter. Retroactive or repeated accrual: the elapsed-time measure moves backwards or the same interval is charged twice, so debt grows without time passing. Unbounded fee: the allocation issues fee claims exceeding what was generated, which is issuance of unbacked claims by another name. Asymmetric application: the generated quantity is added to one side of the ledger and not the other, breaking the fold before any conversion sees it. Denominator timing: the fee claim is computed against a denominator taken at the wrong point in the accrual step, so the fee silently dilutes existing claim holders.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Concretely an accrual routine invoked at the start of state-changing operations, computing an increment from a rate source and an elapsed interval, adding it to both the creditor-side and debtor-side measures, and issuing a fee claim from the increment. Violations live in: an elapsed-time source that is not monotone; an accrual path reachable more than once per interval; a fee computation whose denominator is taken before rather than after the increment (or the reverse) contrary to the declared relation; and a discretization whose truncation error is not bounded, letting repeated small accruals drift from the declared relation.
descriptions.formal_verification: The exactness clause is an equality between the post-state and a declared function of the pre-state, so it is SMT-tractable once the accrual relation is written as an executable reference; the practical difficulty is that the reference is often a discretized approximation whose error must itself be bounded rather than ignored. The bound and monotonicity clauses are ordinary state invariants. Verifying only that some interest was added, without an independent post-state formula, is a common and weak result: it establishes that the transition is reachable, not that it is correct.

formalization.signature: States State; instances M; elapsed-time measure T : State -> Time with ordering <=_T; accrual function Accrue : State x Time -> Q giving the generated quantity; allocation function Alloc : Q x State -> (Q_creditor, Q_fee); debt measure Debt : M x State -> Q; protected-claim measure Protected : M x State -> Q; declared discretization error bound eps.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Exactness:  forall m, s, s', dt . accrualStep(m, s, s', dt)  ->  postState(m, s') = declaredRelation(preState(m, s), Accrue(s, dt), Alloc).
Fee bound:  forall q, s . let (c, f) = Alloc(q, s) in f <= q and c + f = q.
Time monotonicity:  forall s, s' . step(s, s')  ->  T(s) <=_T T(s').
No repeated interval:  forall m, s, s', dt . accrualStep(m, s, s', dt)  ->  dt = T(s) - lastAccrual(m, s) and lastAccrual(m, s') = T(s).
Debt monotonicity under pure accrual:  forall m, s, s' . accrualStep(m, s, s', dt) and dt > 0  ->  Debt(m, s) <= Debt(m, s').
Protected-claim monotonicity:  forall m, s, s' . accrualStep(m, s, s', dt)  ->  Protected(m, s) <= Protected(m, s').
Discretization bound:  the declared relation's deviation from the profile's ideal accrual is bounded by eps, and eps is stated with any result.

temporal_logic.ltl: G( feeBounded and timeNonDecreasing and (accrualStep -> postStateEqualsDeclaredRelation) )

hoare.pre: T(s) = t and lastAccrual(m) = t0 and t >= t0
hoare.post: postState = declaredRelation(preState, Accrue(s, t - t0), Alloc) and lastAccrual(m) = t
fee <= q and creditor + fee = q
no state change: a zero interval generates nothing

formalization.state_machine: Annotate accrual edges with the elapsed interval consumed. The property is that each interval is consumed at most once, that the edge's effect equals the declared relation applied to the source state, and that the fee component of the allocation never exceeds the generated component.
formalization.type_theoretic: The generated quantity as a linear resource produced by an accrual step and consumed exactly once by allocation; the fee claim is typed as a share of that resource, so an allocation exceeding it is not typeable.
formalization.algebraic: Accrual composes over adjacent intervals: accruing over an interval then its successor equals accruing over their concatenation, up to the declared discretization bound. That composition law is what makes a non-monotone or repeated interval a detectable violation.

relationships.note: The generated quantity is applied to aggregate ledgers; fold consistency must survive the accrual step or the exactness clause is checked against a corrupt pre-state.
Fee claims are issued through a conversion; the allocation's fee bound can be defeated by an under-protected conversion direction at the issuance site.
The generated quantity is derived from an external rate source; without that source's call contract the accrual relation has no well-defined input.
Accrual is a sanctioned value-creating flow; this record supplies the term that generic conservation leaves as an undefined issuance.

attack_surface.pattern: a non-monotone time source or a re-enterable accrual path charges the same interval more than once
attack_surface.notes: Time monotonicity and the no-repeated-interval clause together.

attack_surface.pattern: the allocation issues fee claims exceeding the generated quantity
attack_surface.notes: Issuance of unbacked claims. The bound clause is the direct guard.

attack_surface.pattern: the fee claim is computed against a denominator taken at the wrong point of the accrual step, diluting existing claim holders
attack_surface.notes: The declared relation must fix the point; leaving it implicit is where this hides.

attack_surface.pattern: the generated quantity is added to the creditor measure but not the debtor measure, or the reverse
attack_surface.notes: Breaks BPO:0110's fold before any conversion observes it.

attack_surface.pattern: repeated short accruals accumulate truncation error away from the ideal relation
attack_surface.notes: Requires the error bound to be declared and proved, not assumed small.

events: accrual events carrying elapsed interval, generated quantity, and allocation split
metrics: generated quantity minus allocated total (must be the identity)
fee as a share of generated quantity (must respect the declared bound)
cumulative deviation from the ideal accrual relation
invariant_checkpoints: post-accrual: post-state equals the declared relation applied to the pre-state
post-accrual: last-accrual marker advanced to the current time measure
runtime_assertions: assert fee does not exceed the generated quantity
assert a zero elapsed interval produces no state change
assert the time measure never decreases

strategies.notes: Prove the post-state equals a separately written reference relation. Checking only that the transition is reachable and that debt increased is materially weaker and should not be reported as accrual correctness.

strategies.approach: Complete finite reachability with non-zero accrual paths
strategies.notes: Exhaustive over a finite time/quantity profile, with the profile chosen so that non-zero interest and non-zero fee paths are actually reachable. A profile in which the fee is always zero makes the bound clause vacuous.

strategies.approach: Golden-trace regression against an exact reference
strategies.notes: A curated trace reaching a known exact value. Demonstrates the relation on one path; it is not domain-exhaustive and must not be reported as such.
Bound the declared relation's deviation from the profile's ideal accrual over any admissible interval sequence.

testability: a zero elapsed interval is a no-op
the same interval cannot be charged twice across any reachable operation sequence
the fee never exceeds the generated quantity, including at the extremes of the fee parameter
accruing over two adjacent intervals matches accruing over their concatenation within the declared bound

runtime: accrue at the entry of every state-changing operation so no path observes stale balances
advance the last-accrual marker in the same indivisible step as the accrual
assert the fee bound before issuing the fee claim
static: prove the post-state relation against an independent reference
prove the time measure is non-decreasing on every path
prove the fee denominator is taken at the point the declared relation fixes
design_patterns: one accrual routine rather than per-operation inline arithmetic
declare the discretization and its error bound in the specification
make the ideal accrual relation executable for differential testing

assumptions.statement: Arithmetic on accrual intermediates is checked, so the generated quantity cannot wrap.
The elapsed-time measure available to the instance is monotone non-decreasing.
The external rate source terminates and returns a value within its declared range.
The declared discretization is an acceptable approximation of the profile's intended accrual for the intervals the deployment will actually see.

provenance.notes: Deliberately does not fix a rate model, a discretization, or a fee denominator convention — a specialization binds all three. The record's contribution is requiring that the relation be declared and that the fee be bounded by what was generated, which is the clause a generic conservation invariant leaves open.
